Acquisition / Lead economics

Media-only customer acquisition cost

Advertising spend per new paying customer attributed to those advertisements. The restricted cost scope makes this useful for campaign comparisons while keeping it distinct from fully loaded customer acquisition cost.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

Advertising spend per new paying customer attributed to those advertisements. The restricted cost scope makes this useful for campaign comparisons while keeping it distinct from fully loaded customer acquisition cost.

currency / new customer

How we use it

Compare paid-channel efficiency after leads become customers. We show the attribution model and acquisition cohort alongside the result to make campaign decisions reviewable.

Transparent calculationAttributed media spend ÷ new paying customers attributed to that media
media spend6,000
attributed new customers12

6,000 ÷ 12 = 500 currency units of media cost per new attributed customer.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Channel and campaign
  • Customer segment and market
  • Acquisition cohort

Questions we investigate

  • Are customers new and paying?
  • Does attribution match the media cost scope?
  • How does media CAC differ from fully loaded CAC?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Reconcile attributed customers with payment records.
  • Review advertising cost with contribution.
  • Compare media-only and full acquisition economics.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Performance marketing lead
Monthly after attribution and customer status reconcile.

Required data

  • Attributed media spend and currency
  • New attributed paying customer IDs
  • Attribution model and maturity window

Read the measure with context

Zero attributed new customers makes this undefined. It excludes sales and marketing payroll, agencies, software, and overhead. Attribution is an assignment rule and does not prove incremental lift. Long sales cycles require matched cost and customer cohorts.
